searchText: If anyone currently has prysm-besu or prysm-erigon synced on kiln using the latest commits, can you please share your settings? Two days ago, an update broke things for those two pairs as well as prysm-ethereumjs. The only way I could get ethereumjs back online was to run eth and engine on the same port *and* disable `rpcEngineAuth`. the shadow forks are just "dry run" forks that only trigger on the clients configured manually to follow the shadow fork, so that the tests can be repeated multiple times w/o actually forking a real testnet (and "wasting" it if there's a bug that makes the fork fail). Once everyone is happy w/ the shadow forks I presume the next step will be to fork goerli, sepolia, and ropsten (not sure if in that order) and then mainnet. thank you very much for that explanation! all clear now! <@!892053833121923094> thanks a lot for your input on the test coverage. I have addressed your comments and checked what is already done. I am currently working on the transition part, would like to collect more checks from EIPs and consensus specs, then create a separate Transition section incorporating all these checks <@!543900561460822016> IIRC, you have some transition testing scenarios written in some doc, could you please share it? it's right here: https://hackmd.io/@matt/HyH46iOhY

excerpts.author: seamonkey82
excerpts.content: If anyone currently has prysm-besu or prysm-erigon synced on kiln using the latest commits, can you please share your settings?  Two days ago, an update broke things for those two pairs as well as prysm-ethereumjs.  The only way I could get ethereumjs back online was to run eth and engine on the same port *and* disable `rpcEngineAuth`.

Once everyone is happy w/ the shadow forks I presume the next step will be to fork goerli, sepolia, and ropsten (not sure if in that order) and then mainnet.
